title: G1b playback arm regresses 24% on Demo 2 under every clip-hiding mechanism
description:
Found by strides-kyu.3. The shell restructure is free; CONCEALING the clip's <video> is not.

Demo 2 (portrait 4K, 59.94fps — the only test clip whose sampling is throughput-limited), playback
arm (`{"sequentialSampling":{"enabled":false}}`), 5 trials per variant, paired back-to-back against
a throwaway worktree at ab5d185, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro):

  base ab5d185 (old layout, visible)      62 [57..63]
  kyu.3 layout, wrapper left `relative`   61 [56..63]   restructure is FREE
  kyu.3 layout, `fixed` but ON SCREEN     63 [57..64]   `position:fixed` is FREE
  L0  fixed offscreen + inert             47 [46..57]   -24%   (shipped)
  L3  1x1 overflow:hidden window          47 [40..59]   -24%
  L2  -z-20 behind an opaque backdrop     39 [37..47]   -37%
  L1  opacity-0 + -z-10                   34 [33..39]   -45%

Pre-registered gate is +/-10%. Every rung of design.md D2's escalation ladder fails it, and the
ladder's ordering is INVERTED — L0 is jointly the best concealed option, descending is monotonically
worse. "Descend on failure" has nowhere to go, so this is not fixable by picking a rung.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT EARLIER
- G1a passes. It measures an IDLE element with no competing per-frame work; the hidden element does
  still present frames (Demo 2 116 vs visible 118). The failure is proportional, not binary: fewer
  SAMPLES once something contends for the frame budget. D8's "PRIMARY instrument … decisive in
  seconds" is necessary but not sufficient and must always be run with G1b's playback arm.
- Demo 1 (landscape 4K, 25fps) reads 47 -> 47 at every rung — 40ms/frame is enough slack to absorb
  the added per-frame cost. Any gate that measures only Demo 1 reads green through this entire
  failure. Demo 2 must be in the matrix.

BLAST RADIUS (bounded)
Default WebCodecs path untouched: Demo 1 53 -> 53, Demo 2 99 -> 99, bit-identical, `sampling.path`
asserted `'sequential'` vs `'playback'` per arm. The loss lands only where canUseSequentialDecode
returns false — WebM and webcam recordings. That is exactly the population D8's own correction
identified as the one the original G1 was blind to, and the population D1's observational guard
exists to protect.

THE ONE DIRECTION THE DATA SUPPORTS
Keep the element genuinely ON SCREEN while its own analysis is in flight, and conceal it only once
that clip reaches a terminal phase. Both "visible" controls above measure at or above baseline, so
this is the shape that works. It changes what the reader sees during analysis, which is a product
decision — kyu.3 deliberately did not make it. Note it composes with D1's presentation-scoped
looping (kyu.5): "presented" and "must stay visible because it is being sampled" would become two
reasons for the same element to be on screen.

Not yet ruled out and worth measuring before designing anything: whether a genuinely visible but
very small on-screen element (scaled down, not clipped — distinct from L3, which clips a full-size
element) keeps full throughput. If it does, it is a far cheaper answer than a visible-during-
analysis surface.

Repro: node scripts/ab-person-selection.mjs --arm 'playback={"sequentialSampling":{"enabled":false}}'
--clips demo2 --trials 5 --port <free>
close_reason:
RESOLVED by measurement — the cause is on-screen vs off-screen, not any concealment technique, and a genuinely visible element keeps FULL throughput down to at least 60 CSS px.

Demo 2, playback arm, 5 trials/arm, same session, real GPU (ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro), sampling.path='playback' on all 30 trials, commit bf95a1a:

  visible-full (control, 264x470 = 124,256 px painted)   61 [56..62]   —
  visible-full (repeat, 321x570 = 182,756 px)            61 [49..62]   0.0%   PASS
  tiny-120     (67.5x120 = 8,100 px)                     62 [56..63]  +1.6%   PASS
  tiny-60      (33.75x60 = 2,025 px)                     62 [56..63]  +1.6%   PASS
  L0 shipped   (offscreen + inert, 0 px on screen)       49 [48..52] -19.7%   FAIL
  L0 repeat    (end of session)                          47 [46..55] -23.0%   FAIL

NO THRESHOLD. Painted area varies 61x across the three passing arms (2,025 -> 124,256 px) with throughput flat at 61-62. The discontinuity is binary: on screen or not.

The negative control held at the end of the session (47 [46..55], matching this ticket's independently-measured 47 [46..57]) and the positive control reproduced at 61 twice at two different sizes and offsets — so the session COULD resolve the known failure, making its inability to find one in the tiny arms a real null rather than a blind instrument.

RESOLUTION: keep the analysing clip's element genuinely on screen. The navbar strip thumbnail (60-120 CSS px) can simply BE the live element while that clip's analysis is in flight, reverting to the static poster once it reaches a terminal phase. No product compromise, no visible-at-size surface needed. Folded into strides-kyu.4.

title: Fix poster review findings: decoder fan-out and webcam frame-0
description:
Code review of strides-kyu.2 (commit 70b9a8a) returned two ship-blocking findings plus two test gaps against that ticket's own stated acceptance criteria.

## MUST-FIX 1 — N concurrent detached 4K decoders (CONFIRMED)
useClipPoster.ts:41 -> posterFrame.ts:202-231. `useClipPoster` is per-ClipSlot with NO cross-clip serialization, so every clip reaching status:'ready' opens its own detached <video> with preload='auto' over its full blob, CONCURRENTLY, during sampling.

This is the exact hazard the module it borrows from serializes against by construction — extractFrames.ts:474-478: 'Sequential by construction rather than by caller convention: Demo 1 is 3840x2160 and Demo 2 is 2160x3840, so N concurrent detached decoders is not an acceptable amount of memory to hold (design R3).'

Repro: FileUpload sets `multiple` and fires onSelected once per file (FileUpload.tsx:33-35), wired straight to addClip (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:218). Pick 4 files -> 4 addClip in one tick -> 4 ClipSlots mount -> 4 queueMicrotask(load) in one flush -> 4 simultaneous deriveClipPoster, each minting a 4K decoder and seeking it, while clip 1's MoveNet/WebGL sampling loop runs against the shared detector.

kyu.2's live verification was single-clip only, so acceptance criterion 2 ('does not disturb analysis') is UNVERIFIED for the multi-clip path this feature exists to serve.

Fix direction: a module-level promise chain in posterFrame.ts, matching extractSessionEvidence's posture. Serialize by construction, not by caller convention.

## MUST-FIX 2 — every webcam clip posters at frame 0 (CONFIRMED)
posterFrame.ts:126-130. `choosePosterTimestamp` returns 0 for non-finite duration. POSTER_TIMESTAMP_FRACTION's own doc (posterFrame.ts:37-42) says zero is precisely what must be avoided: 'the first frame of a real clip is routinely a fade-in, a black leader, or the runner not yet in shot.'

MediaRecorder WebM reports duration: Infinity — already asserted in-repo at EvidenceGallery.tsx:93-94. useVideoSource.ts:53 copies video.duration verbatim into metadata.durationSec. So: choosePosterTimestamp(Infinity) -> 0 -> seekTo(video, 0) short-circuits to 'already-there' (extractFrames.ts:147), skipping even the presentation wait -> drawImage of frame 0. For a self-recorded run that is the user still walking back from the camera.

Systematic for one of the app's four input modes, and silent. **posterFrame.test.ts:123 tests this case as 'falls back to the first frame' — the test locks in the defect rather than catching it.** Fix the test's intent too.

Fix direction: when duration is unusable, still target a small fixed offset rather than 0 (the existing cap is a natural candidate), degrading gracefully if that seek cannot complete. Do not simply widen the clamp.

## SHOULD-FIX 3 — both MultiClipVideoSession release sites are untested
MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:130 and :187 are exactly what kyu.2's acceptance criterion 5 ('released on clip removal and session reset') names, and MultiClipVideoSession.test.tsx has zero references to poster or releaseClipPoster. Replace either call with a no-op and the suite stays green. useClipPoster.test.ts covers the HOOK's cleanup — a different site, and specifically the one both code comments say they deliberately do NOT rely on. So 'release does not lean on React cleanup ordering' is asserted in prose and nowhere in code. sameClipSession's new `previous.poster === next.poster` line (:67) is likewise uncovered.

## SHOULD-FIX 4 — 'derives once per source' is load-bearing and unasserted
useClipPoster.test.ts never asserts deriveClipPoster's call COUNT (only not.toHaveBeenCalled at :67). ClipSlot reports up on every render and the parent re-renders on every progress tick. It is correct today because all three effect deps are useVideoSource state set once per load — the reviewer traced and confirmed this — but a future change making `metadata` a per-render object would re-decode a 4K clip on every progress tick with no failing test.

## NOT findings — verified correct, do not 'fix' these
- The `clipIds.length > 1` guard at :130 is correct, not a leak. When false, setClipIds refuses the removal, the slot stays mounted, and useClipPoster keeps owning and re-reporting that poster; releasing there would blank a live thumbnail.
- All four release paths fire, including the decode that resolves after teardown. No leak path found.
- The detached decoder is torn down on every path; the object URL is created after both null guards so no path creates one it does not revoke.
- The non-disturbance claim holds transitively — no caller-owned element is reachable.
- sameClipSession still terminates.
- The purity boundary is genuine, not nominal.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Poster derivation is serialized across clips BY CONSTRUCTION, not by caller convention
- [ ] Multi-clip poster path live-verified: 3+ clips added in one file-picker interaction, sampling.detectedFrames still in normal range, numbers recorded
- [ ] A clip with unusable duration (MediaRecorder WebM, duration===Infinity) no longer posters at frame 0
- [ ] posterFrame.test.ts:123's assertion is rewritten to express the intended behavior, not the defect
- [ ] MultiClipVideoSession.test.tsx covers release on clip removal AND on session reset — verified load-bearing by confirming the suite fails when either call is stubbed out
- [ ] useClipPoster.test.ts asserts the derive call COUNT across many re-renders
- [ ] tsc -b, npm test, eslint all clean
notes:
=== ACCURACY NOTE on finding 2's severity — the fix is right, the premise was overstated ===

The review claimed every webcam clip posters at frame 0. Measured during the fix: on Chromium 151, `recorder.start()` with NO timeslice — which is exactly what `WebcamCapture.tsx:203` calls — produces a WebM reporting a FINITE duration. The Infinity case reproduces through `recorder.start(100)` (chunked), which this app does not do.

So finding 2 did NOT reproduce through the app's actual webcam path on that browser/version. It is still a real hazard: the in-repo comment at EvidenceGallery.tsx:93-94 asserts MediaRecorder WebM reports Infinity (measured at some earlier point, possibly a different engine), MediaRecorder duration reporting is a well-known long-standing cross-browser quirk, and `useVideoSource.ts:53` copies `video.duration` verbatim with no guard.

The fix is correct and costs nothing — an unusable duration now targets a 1.0s offset and falls back to frame 0 only if that seek cannot complete. But it is DEFENSIVE hardening against a case not currently observed in this app on this engine, not the repair of a live user-visible defect. Recording this so the next reader does not over-trust the finding's framing.

Finding 1 (decoder fan-out) is unaffected by this note — it was reproduced live, 3 concurrent decoders pre-fix vs 1 post-fix, in the app's real multi-file path.

title: Reconcile the poster spec with the shipped detached-decoder implementation
description:
Wave 1 ran strides-kyu.1 (spec) and strides-kyu.2 (implementation) in PARALLEL. They disagree about how a poster is captured. This is a parallelization cost, not a mistake by either agent — neither could see the other's output.

## The disagreement
`openspec/changes/navbar-clip-shell/specs/video-input/spec.md` 'Poster frame for a loaded clip' says:
  'Deriving the poster SHALL NOT disturb the element's playback: it SHALL NOT seek, play, pause,
   mute, or otherwise write to the video element's playback state. IT CAPTURES WHATEVER FRAME THE
   ELEMENT HAS ALREADY DECODED.'
and its scenario 'A poster appears once a frame is decodable' keys on 'its element has decoded its first frame'.

The shipped implementation (commit 70b9a8a, `src/video/posterFrame.ts` + `useClipPoster.ts`) instead mints a DETACHED <video> from `videoSource.sourceBlob` with its own object URL and decoder, seeks THAT to 10% in (capped at 1s), draws, and tears all three down. `useClipPoster` reads status/sourceBlob/metadata and never `videoRef`.

## Resolution: amend the SPEC, keep the implementation
The spec's real invariant is 'never write to the canonical element's playback state'. The implementation satisfies that MORE strongly than the spec's own mechanism does — it cannot reach the canonical element at all, which is a structural guarantee rather than a discipline. The spec's literal mechanism is also worse in practice:
- The canonical element's already-decoded frame at 'ready' is frame 0, which on real clips is routinely a fade-in or black leader. A strip of black squares is worse than no strip.
- During sampling it is whatever mid-analysis frame happens to be up — non-deterministic, and different every run given this repo's documented frame-timing jitter.

The implementation was live-verified with a paired baseline arm (real GPU, code genuinely stashed for the control): sampling identical at 99/99/0 on Demo 2, Demo 1 detected 53 frames matching CLAUDE.md's documented anchor exactly, wall clock differing ~100ms in both directions. Zero measurable analysis cost.

## What to change
In `navbar-clip-shell/specs/video-input/spec.md`, requirement 'Poster frame for a loaded clip':
- Permit deriving the poster from a separate, short-lived decoder built from the retained source blob, and REQUIRE that the canonical element's playback state is never written to. Keep 'SHALL NOT seek, play, pause, mute, or otherwise write' scoped to the CANONICAL element.
- Adjust the scenario 'A poster appears once a frame is decodable' so it does not mandate capturing from the canonical element.
- KEEP unchanged: no serialization of the poster itself (data URL / blob / object URL / storage); release on removal and reset; the pure sizing/aspect math rule; the null-until-available lifecycle and neutral-placeholder consumer rule.
- Note that an object URL for the transient DECODER is permitted and must be revoked — it is not a serialization of the poster.
- Re-run `openspec validate navbar-clip-shell --strict`.

Also worth adding as a scenario, since it is the stronger guarantee the implementation actually provides: poster derivation never obtains a reference to the canonical element at all.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Spec permits the detached-decoder mechanism and forbids writing to the canonical element's playback state
- [ ] The 'no serialization of the poster' rule survives verbatim in intent, with the transient decoder's object URL explicitly carved out and required to be revoked
- [ ] Release-on-removal/reset and the pure-math rule survive
- [ ] `openspec validate navbar-clip-shell --strict` passes
- [ ] No src/ changes — the implementation is correct as shipped
close_reason: Spec amended to match the shipped detached-decoder implementation. video-input 'Poster frame for a loaded clip' now scopes the no-write rule to the canonical element and permits a derivation-owned transient decoder; added scenarios for 'never reaches the canonical element' and 'transient decoder torn down on every path'; carved the decoder's object URL out of the no-serialization rule while keeping the poster itself covered. design.md D5 rewritten with a revision note recording the parallel-execution cause and the paired-baseline evidence. proposal.md + tasks.md destaled; tasks 2.1-2.6 checked off. Verified choosePosterTimestamp clamps non-finite duration to 0, so D5's webcam duration===Infinity objection is handled. openspec validate --strict passes. Commit e276dd1. No src/ changes.

title: Build the pure per-metric annotation-geometry layer
description:
The core of Epic B. Turn each metric's exemplar into a canvas-free description of what to draw. No rendering in this ticket.

## The coordinate transform (video-native -> output canvas)
  outputSide = max(1, round(min(crop.side, maxOutputSidePx)))   // maxOutputSidePx default 640
  s  = outputSide / crop.side
  cx = (kp.x - crop.x) * s
  cy = (kp.y - crop.y) * s
Note s is round(min(side,640))/side, NOT 640/side — the rounding is in the numerator only, and computeCropRect returns FLOAT sides, so s is not exactly 1 even when side <= 640. No explicit point-mapping helper exists today; the forward transform is only implicit in the 9-arg drawImage at extractFrames.ts:327-337. The exact INVERSE already exists at movenet.ts:88-95 (`toVideoSpaceKeypoints`) — same algebra, opposite direction.

## toDrawOps cannot be reused as-is — three concrete reasons
`toDrawOps(frame): DrawOp[]` (skeletonGeometry.ts:121-164) emits `PointDrawOp {kind,name,x,y,opacity}` / `EdgeDrawOp {kind,from,to,x1,y1,x2,y2,opacity}`, with DETECTED_OPACITY 1 / INTERPOLATED_OPACITY 0.35 and edge opacity = min of endpoints. Reuse the MODEL, but it needs a variant because:
  1. coordinates are video-native with no transform hook (:130)
  2. it draws all 22 SKELETON_EDGES, not the exemplar's cropKeypoints subset — a kneeFlexion crop would get the whole skeleton, nearly all of it outside the crop
  3. no frame-level opacity multiplier: a ghosted pair needs base skeleton at 1.0 and ghost at EVIDENCE_GHOST_OPACITY 0.5, composed with each point's own detected/interpolated opacity

## Per-metric marks (researched from the calcs, not guessed)
- trunkLean: hip-mid -> shoulder-mid segment; VERTICAL ray up from hip-mid; ANGLE ARC at hip-mid between them. This is literally what atan2(dx,-dy) measures (trunkLean.ts:164-173). Two instants, each with its own arc.
- kneeFlexion: hip -> knee -> ankle chain; reference ray = hip->knee extended past the knee; ANGLE ARC at the KNEE vertex. CAUTION: the reported number is 180 - interiorAngle, so the drawn arc is the SUPPLEMENT of the value. Label accordingly. The ghost (extension trough) is legibility context only and carries no measured value (kneeFlexion.ts:69-81) — must not be captioned as measured.
- overstriding: ankle <-> hip-mid; VERTICAL plumb line at hipMid.x; HORIZONTAL caliper plumb->ankle. Not an angle.
- footStrikePattern: knee -> ankle shank; VERTICAL plumb at the knee; HORIZONTAL caliper knee.x->ankle.x, plus the +/-0.05*torso midfoot band as guide lines. Do NOT draw a shank-vs-vertical arc labelled with the value — the quantity is a horizontal offset, not an angle. ONE instant.
- stepWidth / stepWidthCm: ankle + both hips; VERTICAL midline at hipMidX, PER FRAME (a ghosted pair has TWO midlines, not one); HORIZONTAL caliper midline->ankle per instant. For stepWidth the left_hip->right_hip segment IS the normalizer and is drawable in-frame.
- armSwingSymmetry: shoulder -> elbow -> wrist, one side; HORIZONTAL line through the shoulder in each frame; TWO VERTICAL BARS for wrist.y - shoulder.y. Drawing only the two wrist positions would be WRONG — the quantity is a difference of two SHOULDER-RELATIVE offsets (armSwingSymmetry.ts:117).
- bounceCycle (verticalOscillation, verticalOscillationCm, verticalRatio): midpoint marker + HORIZONTAL line at each instant's midpoint-y. See the honesty rule below before adding a caliper label.
- verticalRatio stridePair: hip-mid marker; VERTICAL tick at each hip-mid x; HORIZONTAL caliper between ticks.
- cadence: emits nothing, by design (cadence.ts:118-129, and independently METRICS_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE at evidenceFrames.ts:97).

## HONESTY RULE — the drawn quantity is usually NOT the card's number
Do not label a mark with the metric's reported value unless they are genuinely the same quantity. They usually are not:
- bounceCycle amplitude is a whole-clip least-squares spectral fit with a c+d*t+e*t^2 trend removed (bounceInstants.ts:20-30). The pixel gap between the two ghosted midpoints is NOT the reported amplitude. verticalOscillationCm is further removed still — its fit is over integrated metre deltas from one winning run.
- verticalRatio's value is a quotient across two DIFFERENT exemplars; each image shows one factor.
- armSwingSymmetry's value is a ratio BETWEEN the two images.
- Every torso/hip-width-normalized ratio (overstriding, footStrikePattern, stepWidth) divides by a CLIP-MEDIAN body scale (bodyScale.ts:41, :68) — numerator drawable, denominator not.
- trunkLean and overstriding deliberately select the EXTREME instants (exemplars.ts:44-54) while the card reports a MEDIAN, so the drawn geometry is by construction not the reported number.
Caption marks as what was measured AT THIS INSTANT. This is the same discipline that keeps the spec's ideal-posture prohibition meaningful.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A pure, canvas-free module turns an EvidenceFramePlan into annotation draw ops in output-canvas coordinates
- [ ] The transform is exercised by unit tests including a fractional crop.side (s != 1)
- [ ] Joint layer reuses the skeletonGeometry DrawOp model and preserves detected-vs-interpolated opacity, composed with the base/ghost multiplier
- [ ] Only the exemplar's own keypoints are drawn, not all 22 skeleton edges
- [ ] Per-metric marks match the table above; kneeFlexion's supplement relationship is handled explicitly
- [ ] No mark is labelled with the card's reported value where the drawn quantity differs; metrics with no honestly drawable mark get joints only
- [ ] Zero canvas/DOM references in this module (it must run in jsdom)
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean
notes:
=== CORRECTIONS from the strides-ac9.1 spec pass (source-verified) — these override the description ===

1. **stepWidth's normalizer is HIP WIDTH, not torso length — and this row is the most dangerous, not the safest.**
   The description's per-metric table calls stepWidth safe on the grounds that 'the left_hip->right_hip segment IS the normalizer and is drawable in-frame'. That is WRONG. stepWidth divides by `estimateHipWidth`'s CLIP-MEDIAN `hipWidthPx` (stepWidth.ts:224, bodyScale.ts:56-68 — deliberately a separate function from estimateBodyScale per bodyScale.ts:46-55).
   The hip segment visible in the picture is THAT FRAME'S hip width. The value used the CLIP MEDIAN. So a reader who measures the drawn segment and divides gets a different number than the card shows — a drawable-LOOKING denominator that is not the one used. Draw the segment, but do NOT label the quotient.

2. **trunkLean's sign flips with direction of travel.** trunkLean.ts:171-173 multiplies by travelDirection. On a right-to-left runner the sign of the tilt visible on screen is the OPPOSITE of the sign the card reports. An arc labelled with the card's value would point the wrong way — not merely be imprecise. This is now a spec scenario in the inline-annotated-evidence change.

3. armSwingSymmetry's reported value is computed at armSwingSymmetry.ts:271, not :117. (:117 is the per-side half-swing excursion, which is the drawable part.)

4. stepWidthCm has NO clip-median denominator — it divides by per-frame `frame.pixelsPerMeter` (stepWidthCm.ts:248). Still not drawable (a MediaPipe world-landmark calibration is not a visible length), so same no-label rule, different reason.

Read `openspec/changes/inline-annotated-evidence/design.md` D2 for the verified per-metric table — prefer it over the description's table where they disagree.
=== DECISION YOU MUST MAKE — grafted metrics resolve annotation off the WRONG detector's frames ===
From the strides-ac9.6 code review. CONFIRMED mechanism, not yet user-visible, and it lands squarely in this ticket.

`resolveOutwardSigns`'s doc claims it is 'stepWidth.ts:222-223 verbatim, not an approximation'. True for the PRIMARY-pass stepWidth. NOT true for **stepWidthCm** and **verticalOscillationCm**, which arrive by graft from the background MediaPipe scale pass.

scalePassGraft.ts:43-50 records that grafted exemplars carry the SCALE PASS's instants while 'the only frames any consumer holds are the primary pass's', and EvidenceGallery.tsx:204 duly hands planClipEvidence `input.frames = clip.analysis.robustFrames` (MoveNet) alongside the grafted heuristics. So instantPlan resolves those exemplars' joint positions AND hip polarity off a MoveNet frame snapped within tolerance — never the MediaPipe frame the metric actually measured.

Concrete failure: front-view clip, MoveNet primary, scale pass 'agreed' (so dropGraftedExemplars does not fire). stepWidthCm selects a right-foot strike where MediaPipe put right_hip 4px right of left_hip -> outwardSign +1, a positive 'own side' offset. MoveNet's frame at the nearest sampled timestamp puts the hips 2px the other way — a coin flip at that separation, and near-frontal instants are exactly where step-width strikes live. The plan then carries {left:+1, right:-1}, the INVERSE of what the metric used, and your caliper labels a crossover strike as landing on its own side — contradicting the card's own crossover caveat (stepWidth.ts:273-277) in the same viewport.

Live-reachable: this repo's measurements record verticalOscillationCm planning an exemplar post-graft on all three test clips.

Not introduced by ac9.6 — it widened a documented, accepted seam that previously carried only a coarse crop box, where a few pixels are invisible. ac9.6 is the first to push a POLARITY through it.

DECIDE, and record the decision: (a) draw no signed/oriented mark for grafted metrics, (b) draw joints only for them, or (c) accept it with a stated argument for why the divergence cannot flip a sign in practice. Do NOT let this be discovered at draw time. Whichever you pick, correct resolveOutwardSigns' 'verbatim' doc comment to name the graft exception.
close_reason: Annotation layer shipped as src/results/evidenceAnnotations.ts. planEvidenceAnnotations(plan, maxOutputSidePx) emits flat ops carrying layer ('joint'|'measurement'), instant ('base'|'ghost'|'pair') and a composed opacity, ALL in output-canvas space via a single toEvidenceOutputSpace call site that a hygiene test pins. Dispatch is on exemplar KIND, not MetricId (bounceCycle is shared by three metrics, stepWidthStrike by two). Grafted-metric divergence resolved as option (a): polarity suppressed, geometry kept — verticalOscillationCm stays op-for-op identical to verticalOscillation, stepWidthCm's caliper draws as the unsigned span it honestly is. resolveOutwardSigns' 'verbatim' doc corrected. Ghost multiplier composes as pointOpacity x frameMultiplier, all four combinations asserted. No numeric labels anywhere, per the honesty requirement. Two deviations from the ticket, both recorded in design D12: the midfoot band is DROPPED (its half-width is a clip-median torso length and a band around the knee reads as a target zone, which this change's own spec forbids), and no caliper is emitted without a per-instant side (filed as a follow-up rather than inferred from cropKeypoints array order). 78 files / 1118 tests, tsc + eslint + openspec --strict green, nothing under src/heuristics/ touched.

title: Thread keypoints and measurement sign into the evidence plan
description:
Plumbing prerequisite. Nothing in Epic B can draw a joint or an oriented caliper until this lands.

## Gap 1 — the plan drops the keypoints
`EvidenceFramePlan` (evidenceFrames.ts:139-154) retains only `{metric, kind, side?, quality, label, base:{timestamp,opacity}, ghost, crop, demotedFromPair}`. No RobustPoseFrame, no keypoint positions, and `cropKeypoints` is consumed inside `planExemplarFrames` (:404-429) and then DROPPED.

`robustFrames` is also not threaded into the extractor at all: `ClipEvidenceInput = { sourceBlob, plan }` (extractFrames.ts:121-124), and EvidenceGallery has `input.frames` in scope (:57, :92) but passes only `{sourceBlob, plan}` (:218).

Three viable seams. PREFER THE FIRST — `planExemplarFrames` already holds both RobustPoseFrames at :401-410, so resolving there keeps everything in the pure, unit-testable half exactly as the module already does for crop rects:
  a) resolve positions (or DrawOps) into EvidenceFramePlan during planning  <-- preferred
  b) carry cropKeypoints forward and re-resolve at draw time
  c) add frames to ClipEvidenceInput and resolve in extractFrames.ts

Resolution itself is exact: `base.timestamp`/`ghost.timestamp` are the SAMPLED frame's own timestamp (evidenceFrames.ts:438-445), so `findNearestFrame` returns exactly that frame object. Note `resolvePoint` (keypoints.ts:23-30) treats 'detected' AND 'interpolated' as resolvable; only 'unrecoverable' is null — preserve that distinction, the thumbnails should show it.

## Gap 2 — the sign is missing
`travelDirection` (±1) and `outwardSign` determine the SIGN of every offset metric — overstriding.ts:177, footStrikePattern.ts:192, trunkLean.ts:171, strideLength.ts:182, stepWidth.ts:222-223. NEITHER is carried on `MetricExemplar` nor `EvidenceFramePlan`.

Consequence: a caliper or arrow claiming 'ahead of the hip' vs 'behind', or 'own side' vs 'crossed over', CANNOT be oriented from the plan today. Without this, an overstriding mark can be drawn pointing the wrong way on a right-to-left runner and nothing will catch it.

Thread whichever of these the annotation layer needs. Keep it canvas-free — jsdom has no canvas.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Both instants' keypoint positions are resolvable by the draw layer, with detected-vs-interpolated status preserved
- [ ] travelDirection and/or outwardSign are available wherever a signed mark is drawn

title: EvidenceInstantPlan carries no per-instant side, blocking two calipers
description:
Real gap in strides-ac9.6's seam, found by strides-ac9.7. Not a styling call.

Two exemplar kinds need to know WHICH instant's ankle was the measured one, and the plan cannot say:
- `overstrideRange` pair — loses its ankleOffsetCaliper
- `stepWidthStrike` pair — loses its ankleOffsetCaliper

The PAIR is the common case for both metrics, so this is the majority path, not an edge.

`MetricExemplar.side` is present only when BOTH instants share a side. stepWidth's pair is deliberately constructed from adjacent OPPOSITE-side strikes (exemplars.ts:207-224, stepWidth.ts:93-95), so it never carries one. overstriding's side is present only when both extremes happen to be the same foot (overstriding.ts:101).

ac9.7 REFUSED to infer it from cropKeypoints ordering. That was correct: the base's ankle is ordered first, but that is a private detail of two metric modules, and reading it would make 'which foot was measured' a silent function of an array order nobody tests.

FIX: resolve a per-instant side in `planExemplarFrames`, alongside the keypoint positions ac9.6 already resolves there. The information exists at that point — the metric knows which ankle it measured; it is simply dropped before the plan is built. Add it to `EvidenceInstantPlan`.

Check whether this needs a form-heuristics delta: if the side must ride on MetricExemplar rather than being derivable in the plan, `openspec/specs/form-heuristics/spec.md:1256-1262` ('An exemplar SHALL additionally carry: ...') must be MODIFIED in the same pass — design D8's named condition. Reuse the EXACT existing requirement title text.

- [ ] EvidenceInstantPlan carries the measured side per instant, where one exists
- [ ] overstriding and stepWidth PAIR exemplars emit their ankleOffsetCaliper
- [ ] The side is resolved, never inferred from cropKeypoints array order
- [ ] form-heuristics delta filed if and only if the exemplar contract had to widen
- [ ] tsc -b, npm test, eslint clean

Route: it had to ride on MetricExemplar — the fact is NOT derivable in the plan from what the exemplar carried, since the only trace of which ankle was measured was cropKeypoints ordering, and ac9.7's refusal to read that stands (pinned by a test that gives the crop set the opposite leading ankle and asserts the stated side still wins). title: Evidence extraction fans out to 3 concurrent detached 4K decoders
description:
Measured live during strides-kyu.11's multi-clip verification (headless Chromium, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro, 4-clip session: Demo 1 + 3 files picked in one interaction).

A driver-side probe counted detached <video> decoders — a <video> that gets `src` assigned while disconnected, which is exactly and only what posterFrame.ts:264 and extractFrames.ts:451 do. Attribution was by stack trace at the assignment.

    PEAK CONCURRENT BY OWNER: {"poster": 1, "evidence": 3}

`extractSessionEvidence` (extractFrames.ts:476-485) is sequential WITHIN one call, by construction and by design (its own doc names the 4K memory reason). But EvidenceGallery starts a NEW extraction pass whenever its input signature changes, and nothing serializes those passes against each other. CLAUDE.md already documents the re-extraction trigger: on a MoveNet-primary run the background MediaPipe scale pass grafts verticalOscillationCm after phase:'ready', which changes the signature and correctly triggers re-extraction — that is why two [evidence-coverage] lines appear per run.

With N clips, each overlapping pass holds one decoder, so overlapping passes multiply. Measured timeline (fixed poster arm):

    open #7  [evidence] @14220ms  evidence=1
    open #8  [evidence] @14221ms  evidence=2
    open #9  [evidence] @15291ms  evidence=3   <-- three 4K decoders open at once
    ...
    never-closed=3 at teardown

Also note 3 decoders were still open when the page was torn down, in both arms.

This is the same hazard strides-kyu.11 fixed for posters, one module over. The poster fix put the ordering inside deriveClipPoster (a module-level promise chain) precisely because N independent callers cannot serialize themselves; extractSessionEvidence has the same problem one level up — its own loop only orders the clips within a single call.

Not fixed under strides-kyu.11: that ticket's boundaries explicitly excluded EvidenceGallery.tsx, evidenceFrames.ts and extractFrames.ts as owned by a different epic.

Suggested direction: either a module-level chain in extractFrames.ts covering extractSessionEvidence the way posterFrame.ts:249 covers deriveClipPoster, or have EvidenceGallery abandon an in-flight pass before starting a new one (which would also fix the never-closed decoders).

Repro driver archived at scratchpad/multiclip-poster-drive.mjs.

title: Draw the annotation layer onto the evidence canvas
description:
The impure half: take the annotation draw ops from strides-ac9.7 and render them onto the extracted evidence canvas.

## Where
`extractFrame` (extractFrames.ts:342-380) creates the canvas and calls `drawInstant` (:309-340) for base then ghost. Annotation is drawn after the photographic layers.

## KNOWN TRAP — globalAlpha leaks
`drawInstant` sets `ctx.globalAlpha = instant.opacity` (extractFrames.ts:326) and `extractFrame` NEVER RESETS IT before returning (:366-377). Any annotation drawn on that context after a ghosted pair silently inherits globalAlpha = 0.5. Reset explicitly; do not rely on the current value.

These are small thumbnails, not 14rem gallery figures. Stroke widths, point radii and any text must be sized against the OUTPUT canvas, not assumed from SkeletonOverlay's constants (SKELETON_COLOR '#22d3ee', POINT_RADIUS_PX 6, STROKE_WIDTH_PX 3 — sized for a full-size video overlay). The annotation must survive being displayed small; verify by looking at it, not by reasoning about it.

The joint layer and the measurement layer need to be visually separable — a reader should be able to tell 'these are the detected joints' from 'this is the thing that was measured'.

## Preserve
- Canvas element stays in memory and is adopted into the DOM directly; no toDataURL, no toBlob, no download path (results-view spec L688; the deliberate absence is documented at EvidenceGallery.tsx:283-287).
- One detached decoder at a time, object URL owned and revoked (extractFrames.ts:443-486).

title: Assess annotation misregistration from the 2-frame evidence seek offset (gh #69)
description:
This epic makes an existing latent bug newly VISIBLE, which is why it is scoped here rather than left on the GitHub backlog.

## The measured bug (GitHub #69, not hypothesised)
`sequentialSampling` defaults on, so most MP4s sample through WebCodecs where `robustFrames[].timestamp` is raw `sample.cts / sample.timescale` (src/video/mp4Demux.ts:174) with NO edit-list adjustment, while `HTMLVideoElement.currentTime` IS adjusted. The evidence extractor seeks a detached <video> to the planned timestamp, so every extracted frame lands late by the clip's own `elst media_time / mediaTimescale`. Ground-truthed by ffmpeg/PSNR argmax: +2 frames on all three test clips (0.0800s on Demo 1 at 25fps; 0.033367s on Demo 2 at 59.94fps; 0.033333s on the 60fps multiperson clip). Measures EXACTLY 0 under `{ sequentialSampling: { enabled: false } }` — so it is isolated to the WebCodecs domain, not to seeking.

## Why it matters now and did not before
Today's evidence images are unannotated photographs; a 2-frame offset is invisible. Once joints are drawn from the SAMPLED frame's keypoints onto an image that is 2 frames later, the skeleton floats off the body — 80ms on Demo 1 is ~12% of a step cycle, and a runner's limbs move a lot in 80ms. The annotation will look broken even though the numbers are right.

## Do not just pick a constant
`DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_SEEK_OFFSET_SECONDS` is 0 (extractFrames.ts:80) and #69 is explicit that the correct value is per-clip AND per-sampler: it must be exactly 0 for every WebM/webcam clip and every MP4 where `canUseSequentialDecode` says no. Any single constant is wrong on two of three test clips. #69 carries two real candidate fixes: plumb a per-clip offset using `src/video/containerTiming.ts`'s existing `elst` parser, or align the domains at the demuxer.

## Scope of THIS ticket
Decide, with measurement, whether annotation is acceptable at the current offset. If not, implement one of #69's two fixes. Measure misregistration in PIXELS on a real clip, not in frames — that is the number that decides it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Misregistration quantified in pixels on Demo 1 and Demo 2 with annotation drawn
- [ ] A decision is recorded: acceptable as-is, or fixed — with the measurement behind it
- [ ] If fixed: correct on WebCodecs MP4s AND exactly 0 on WebM/webcam clips and non-sequential-decode MP4s
- [ ] No single global constant is introduced as the fix
- [ ] GitHub #69 updated with the outcome (do not close it without the user's say-so)

The single most important clause to get right, at L746 inside the gallery requirement:
  'The system SHALL NOT draw a skeleton, angle arc, reference line, or any other annotation over an
   extracted image, and SHALL NOT overlay any reference or ideal posture'
That sentence contains TWO prohibitions. Reverse the FIRST (annotating detected/measured geometry is now required). KEEP THE SECOND, explicitly and in the new requirement's own words: no reference posture, no ideal, no target overlay. Thumbnails show what was measured on this runner, never something to match. If the new spec silently drops the second half, the epic has quietly changed what the product claims.

KEEP AND EXTEND, do not rewrite: 'Evidence frames are planned purely, then extracted from a detached video element' (L648). Its purity rule ('the decision half SHALL be pure... no DOM, no canvas, no video element') now extends to annotation geometry.

Also spec: thumbnail sizing/placement in the card (below description on mobile, right on desktop), and that annotation is drawn only for metrics whose quantity is actually drawable on a still — see the per-metric determination in strides-ac9.2.

notes:
CORRECTION to the description: the per-metric drawable-geometry determination is in strides-ac9.7, not strides-ac9.2 (ac9.2 is the card layout ticket).

## Third thing the spec must say — surfaced by research after this ticket was written

The spec must state that a mark is NOT labelled with the card's reported value unless the drawn quantity IS that value. Researched against the calcs, they usually differ:

- bounceCycle amplitude (verticalOscillation, verticalOscillationCm, verticalRatio) is a whole-clip least-squares spectral fit with a c+d*t+e*t^2 trend removed (bounceInstants.ts:20-30). The pixel gap between the two ghosted midpoints is NOT the reported amplitude.
- verticalRatio's value is a quotient across two DIFFERENT exemplars; each image shows one factor only.
- armSwingSymmetry's value is a ratio BETWEEN its two images; neither image shows it.
- overstriding, footStrikePattern, stepWidth all divide by a CLIP-MEDIAN body scale (bodyScale.ts:41, :68). Numerator drawable, denominator not.
- trunkLean and overstriding deliberately select EXTREME instants (exemplars.ts:44-54) while the card reports a MEDIAN — so the drawn geometry is by construction not the reported number.
- kneeFlexion reports 180 - interiorAngle, so a drawn interior arc is the SUPPLEMENT of the value.

This is the same discipline that makes the surviving ideal-posture prohibition meaningful: the images must not overclaim. Spec it as 'annotation depicts what was measured at the depicted instant', not 'annotation depicts the reported value'.

Also worth specing: cadence emits no evidence by design and is enforced in two independent places (cadence.ts:118-129 and METRICS_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE at evidenceFrames.ts:97).

description:

One thumbnail per clip, each showing that clip's OWN processing progress as an overlay on the thumbnail.

## The progress data already exists — do not build a new state machine
Per-clip `VideoAnalysisState` carries its own `phase` and `progress` (src/results/types.ts:39-59), one instance per clip via ClipSlot.tsx:51, already collected by the parent as `clipStates: Record<string, ClipSession>` (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:76). Read that.

Today progress is rendered GLOBALLY from the aggregate in ResultsView.tsx:97-123 ('Analyzing… 42%' / 'Processing results…' / 'Analysis complete.'). Per-clip progress has never been rendered anywhere except the 'Queued — waiting for another clip to finish analyzing…' line at ClipSlot.tsx:106-108.

Phases to represent: 'idle' | 'sampling' | 'processing' | 'ready' | 'error' (src/results/types.ts:6). A queued clip (one not currently holding the shared detector) needs a distinct visual from an actively-sampling one — only one clip holds the detector at a time (multiClipAnalysis.ts:163-172).

- [ ] Clip strip renders in the navbar beside the wordmark, one thumbnail per clip
- [ ] Each thumbnail shows that clip's own progress, sourced from its per-clip VideoAnalysisState
- [ ] Sampling / processing / ready / error / queued are visually distinguishable, and by more than color alone
- [ ] Progress is available to assistive tech as text, not graphic-only
- [ ] Strip is usable at narrow widths (overflow/scroll rather than wrapping the navbar)
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean
notes:
=== SCOPE BOUNDARY from the strides-kyu.1 spec pass ===
Only the PER-CLIP progress percentages move to the strip. The session-level 'Analysis complete.' line and the scale-pass narration ('Measuring more metrics with a second look at the clip…' etc.) STAY in ResultsView — results-view's 'The centimetre card reflects scale-pass progress' requires that line to be always-visible, and this epic never meant to touch it. Do not delete ResultsView.tsx:97-123 wholesale.
=== THE STRIP THUMBNAIL MUST BE THE LIVE ELEMENT WHILE THAT CLIP IS ANALYSING ===
This is now a correctness requirement, not a styling choice. It resolves strides-kyu.13 (P0).

Measured: concealing a clip's <video> costs ~20-24% of sampled frames on the playback path (WebM/webcam). A genuinely VISIBLE element keeps full throughput down to at least 60 CSS px on its longest side — 62 vs a visible control's 61, versus 47-49 concealed — with NO threshold across a 61x range of painted area. On screen or not is the only variable that matters.

So: while a clip's analysis is in flight, its strip entry hosts that clip's real, on-screen, painting <video>. Once it reaches a terminal phase, the entry shows the static poster (strides-kyu.2) and the element may be concealed again. Progress renders over it either way.

TWO TRAPS the measurement hit, both of which read as healthy if you check the wrong thing:
1. **The sticky header silently occludes the top of the page.** A 120px element at top-0 is mostly buried under the ~86px header — a partial concealment that measures like a failure while every class name looks right. getBoundingClientRect reads perfectly healthy in that case. VERIFY PIXELS: screenshot a crop of the video's own rect during analysis and confirm you see the runner, not header text.
2. **elementFromPoint is useless for this check.** `inert` removes the subtree from hit-testing while leaving it fully rendered, so the hit test returns whatever is behind the video even when the video is plainly visible.
Also: trial 1 of every harness invocation reads low despite the warm-up navigation — it inflates the range but not the median.

Note this composes with D1's presentation-scoped looping (strides-kyu.5): 'presented' and 'must be on screen because it is being sampled' become two independent reasons for the same element to be visible.

title: Evidence moves inline into annotated metric-card thumbnails
description:
Dissolve the standalone evidence gallery into the metric cards, and annotate each image with the
geometry the metric was actually derived from.

## Target end state
- Each metric card embeds its own image evidence inline: below the description on mobile, to the RIGHT
  of it on desktop.
- Evidence images become small thumbnails (today they are 14rem-wide gallery figures).
- Each thumbnail is ANNOTATED: the detected joints, plus the specific measurement geometry that metric
  computes (e.g. trunkLean = torso vector + vertical reference + angle arc; kneeFlexion = hip-knee-ankle
  chain + angle arc; stepWidth = lateral ankle separation caliper).
- `EvidenceGallery.tsx` is REPLACED by this, not kept alongside. Decided — do not re-litigate.

## Spec reversal — this is deliberate, not an oversight
`openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md` L746 currently states:
  "The system SHALL NOT draw a skeleton, angle arc, reference line, or any other annotation over an
   extracted image"
This epic reverses exactly that clause. IMPORTANT: reverse ONLY the ban on annotating detected/measured
geometry. The adjacent ban on overlaying a REFERENCE OR IDEAL POSTURE STAYS — thumbnails show what was
measured, never a target to match.

Also reversing: L735 "An evidence gallery renders below the results, grouped by metric" (full reversal —
prefer REMOVE with Reason/Migration + ADD under a fresh name, per CLAUDE.md), and L770 "Metric cards
deep-link to their evidence, and are otherwise unchanged" (no deep link; evidence is in the card).

KEEP AND EXTEND, do not rewrite: L648 "Evidence frames are planned purely, then extracted from a
detached video element". It already computes crops in video-native pixel space from the exemplar's
named keypoints — exactly the data the joint overlay needs.

## HARD CONSTRAINTS
1. jsdom in the unit suite has NO canvas (`getContext()` unimplemented; the repo deliberately refuses the
   `canvas` npm package — see src/test/canvasTestUtils.ts). Annotation geometry MUST live in a pure,
   canvas-free, unit-testable layer; only the final draw touches a rendering context. This mirrors the
   existing rule at results-view L655.
2. Extracted images stay in-memory for the session only — no data URL, no blob, no download, no
   persistence (results-view L688). Today the canvas ELEMENT is adopted into the DOM via
   `replaceChildren` (EvidenceGallery.tsx:296-316); `toDataURL`/`toBlob` are deliberately absent.
3. Evidence must never enter the `[analysis-diagnostics]` console payload (results-view L795) — its
   shape is a live-verification harness contract.

## Reuse, don't reinvent
`src/results/skeletonGeometry.ts` already emits pure point/edge DRAW OPS off `SKELETON_EDGES` with a
detected-vs-interpolated opacity distinction (`toDrawOps`). Reuse that model for the joint layer. Do NOT
write a second skeleton renderer. Note `SkeletonOverlay` the COMPONENT is coupled to a live `<video>`
and its media events — it cannot render against a static image; the reusable half is `toDrawOps`.

## Layout note
`MetricsPanel`'s card grid already uses CONTAINER queries (`@container`, `@lg:grid-cols-2`,
`@3xl:grid-cols-3` — MetricsPanel.tsx:288), the only container-query usage in the app. The
"below on mobile / right on desktop" split inside a card is a per-CARD container query, not a viewport
media query.

## Related (context only, do not close)
- GitHub #71 "Two evidence ghosts are unreadable" — whole-frame crops on far-apart pairs, and bystanders
  inside the 320px crop floor. Directly relevant: thumbnails are SMALLER, so crop quality matters more,
  and joint annotation makes a wrong-subject crop visible. Assess whether this epic subsumes part of it.
- GitHub #70 "extreme-role 1.5-MAD gate unreachable for overstriding" — overstriding emits no evidence on
  any clip measured, so that card gets no thumbnail regardless.
- GitHub #69 "Evidence seek lands 2 frames late on every MP4" — REAL INTERACTION: annotation drawn from
  sampled-frame keypoints onto a 2-frames-late image will be visibly misregistered. Joints will appear
  to float off the body. This epic makes an existing latent bug newly visible.

title: Clips live in the top navbar
description:
Move clip management out of the page body and into the top navbar, next to the "Strides" wordmark.

## Target end state
- A clip strip in the navbar: one thumbnail per clip.
- A quick action in the navbar to record/upload another clip. It replaces the in-body "Add another clip" block once >=1 clip exists.
- Clicking a clip thumbnail opens a modal with that clip's video preview + the pose skeleton/wireframe overlay.
- Per-clip processing progress renders as an overlay ON that clip's navbar thumbnail — not as a separate global banner.
- Zero clips keeps a full-page picker; it collapses into the navbar quick-action once a clip exists.

## Why this is a restructure, not a re-style
Today `MultiClipVideoSession` renders every clip as a full-height `ClipSlot` stacked in a left column,
with a single GLOBAL aggregate progress line in `ResultsView`. There is no clip list UI, no tab bar, no
selector, and no per-clip label or thumbnail anywhere in the model — clips are positional only
(`ClipSession = { clipId, videoSource, analysis }`, src/results/multiClipAnalysis.ts:18-22).

## HARD CONSTRAINT — read before touching anything
Sampling reads frames off a live, PLAYING `<video>` element. Clip video elements MUST stay mounted while
analysing. Do NOT render them only when the modal is open — the modal reveals an already-mounted element.
Getting this wrong silently breaks analysis with no type or test error.

## Spec work
One openspec change covering this epic. Affected capabilities: `results-view`, `video-input`,
`multi-clip-analysis`. Notably `results-view` L174 "Video loops with overlay once analysis is ready"
needs revisiting — a hidden looping video per clip burns GPU, so the loop should likely be scoped to
modal-open.

## Known landmines
- The sticky header height is hardcoded as `86px` in three places (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:182,203)
  and `150px` in VideoInputPanel.tsx:132. A taller navbar breaks all four.
- `e2e/multiPersonAcquisition.spec.ts` drives real selectors this redesign moves:
  `getByRole('button', {name:'Upload'})`, `locator('input[type=file]')`, `getByText(/analysis complete/i)`.

## Related (context only, do not close)
GitHub #23 "Make results layout sticky" is SUPERSEDED by this epic — the two-column video/metrics
layout goes away entirely. Recommend closing it as superseded; that call is the user's.

title: Grafted exemplars carry the scale pass's instants but not its frames
description:
The root cause behind strides-ac9.7's option-(a) workaround. Filed so the workaround is not mistaken for a fix.

scalePassGraft.ts:43-50 records the seam plainly: a grafted exemplar carries the SCALE PASS's instants, but 'the only frames any consumer holds are the primary pass's'. So stepWidthCm and verticalOscillationCm get their joint positions and hip polarity resolved off a MoveNet frame snapped within tolerance — never the MediaPipe frame that actually measured them.

At a near-frontal step-width strike the two hips sit a few pixels apart and the two detectors can order them oppositely, so the plan can carry the INVERSE polarity, labelling a crossover strike as landing on its own side — contradicting stepWidth.ts:273-277's own crossover caveat in the same viewport.

ac9.7 mitigated by suppressing POLARITY (not geometry) for GRAFTED_METRICS. That is correct and cheap, but it is a workaround at the consumer, not a fix at the seam.

The clean fixes, per ac9.7: either a grafted exemplar carries its own pass's frames, or the graft drops when no primary frame corroborates it. Both are scalePassGraft.ts's business, and both are larger than any ticket in epic strides-ac9.

Note this seam previously carried only a coarse crop box, where a few pixels are invisible. ac9.6 was the first change to push a polarity through it — so the seam got riskier without anyone widening it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A grafted metric's annotation geometry derives from the frames that measured it, or the graft is dropped when unsupported
- [ ] ac9.7's GRAFTED_METRICS polarity suppression can be removed, or is documented as permanently correct
- [ ] Live-verified on a front-view clip where the scale pass reports 'agreed'

title: Derive the header offset instead of hardcoding 86px and 150px
description:
The sticky header's height is hardcoded in four places and derived from nothing:
- MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:182 — `lg:top-[86px]`
- MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:203 — `lg:max-h-[calc(100vh-86px)]`

title: Extract shared <video> primitives out of extractFrames.ts
description:
Review finding 4 from strides-kyu.2, deferred as a follow-up rather than blocking the epic.

posterFrame.ts imports `seekTo`/`waitForPresentedFrame` from extractFrames.ts (sound — both are generic <video> primitives carrying no evidence-epic policy) but then RE-IMPLEMENTS a third, `waitForDecodedData` (posterFrame.ts:133-156), byte-for-byte identical to extractFrames.ts:252-278. Plus a duplicate HAVE_CURRENT_DATA (:59 vs extractFrames.ts:83), a duplicate timeout constant (POSTER_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS vs LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS, same 10000, near-identical doc), and a deriveClipPoster try/finally teardown duplicating extractClipEvidence's comment-for-comment.

Cost: a fix to the decoder-teardown sequence or the readiness wait must now be made twice, and only one site is reachable by grepping the other's imports.

Fix: lift the four primitives into a shared `src/video/videoElement.ts` that both import. This removes the coupling entirely rather than undoing the import.

Second reason to do it: extractFrames.ts:28 states 'Runs strictly after phase: ready, never inside the sampling loop.' useClipPoster deliberately runs its borrowed halves DURING sampling (useClipPoster.ts:20-25). That choice is argued and reasonable, but it makes the borrowed module's stated invariant false for one of its consumers.

Also fold in review finding 5 (minor): deriveClipPoster's doc claims 'every failure is a null, never a throw' (posterFrame.ts:164) but :217-230 is try/finally with no catch, and useClipPoster.ts:41 has no rejection handler. Either add the catch or correct the doc. Note EvidenceGallery.tsx:416 has the identical shape, so this is a repo-wide pattern rather than a new deviation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The four duplicated primitives live in one shared module imported by both consumers
- [ ] No behavior change; tsc -b, npm test, eslint clean
- [ ] deriveClipPoster's stated never-throws contract and its code agree

title: Aggregate multi-clip progress becomes a value with no consumer
description:
Follow-up surfaced by the navbar-clip-shell spec pass, deliberately left out of scope there.

`openspec/specs/multi-clip-analysis/spec.md` 'Aggregate multi-clip analysis state' specifies `progress` as the mean of every clip's own progress. Once per-clip progress renders on navbar thumbnails (strides-kyu.4), nothing renders the aggregate mean.

The requirement is not FALSE — `computeAggregateAnalysisState` still computes it — but it now describes a value with no consumer. The spec pass left it alone rather than modify a requirement outside its remit.

Decide: drop the field (and its spec clause), or keep it and document why. Low priority, no user-visible effect either way.
